subject: Reasoning
topic: Number Series — Patterns, Sequences and Missing Terms (W10)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Rule: each term is double the previous (×2). 2→4→8→16→32→64. These are powers of 2: 2¹, 2², 2³, 2⁴, 2⁵, 2⁶. Trap: 48 adds 16 (wrong); 56 adds 24 (wrong). Verify: 32×2 = 64.

C is correct. Rule: perfect squares — n². 1=1², 4=2², 9=3², 16=4², 25=5², next = 6²=36. Trap: 49=7² (skips 6²); 30 is not a perfect square; 32 is a power of 2 (wrong pattern). Differences: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 (consecutive odd numbers — also identifies the pattern).

C is correct. This is the Fibonacci sequence: each term = sum of the two preceding terms. 2+3=5, 3+5=8, 5+8=13, 8+13=21, 13+21=34. Trap: 29=21+8 (skips one step); 32 adds 11 (wrong); 37=21+16 (wrong).

C is correct. Rule: each term = 2×(previous term) + 1. 5×2+1=11, 11×2+1=23, 23×2+1=47, 47×2+1=95, 95×2+1=191. Trap: 143 adds 48 (wrong); 185 computes 95×2−5 (wrong); 201 adds 106 (wrong). This is a common SSC pattern — look for 2n+1 relationships.

B is correct. Differences: 10−7=3, 14−10=4, 19−14=5, 25−19=6 → differences increase by 1 each time. Next difference = 7. 25+7=32. Trap: 30=25+5 (repeats a previous difference); 33=25+8 (skips a step); 35 adds 10 (wrong).

C is correct. Differences: 3, 5, 7, ?, 11 — the differences are consecutive odd numbers. Missing difference = 9. 19+9 = 28. Verify: 28+11=39 ✓. Trap: 26=19+7 (repeats the previous difference); 30=19+11 (skips a step and uses next difference).
C is correct. Rule: perfect cubes — n³. 1=1³, 8=2³, 27=3³, 64=4³, 125=5³, next = 6³=216. Trap: 196=14² (perfect square, not cube); 225=15² (wrong); 180 is neither. Verify: 6×6×6 = 216.

C is correct. Rule: n(n+1) — product of consecutive integers. 1×2=2, 2×3=6, 3×4=12, 4×5=20, 5×6=30, 6×7=42, 7×8=56. Alternative: differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 (even numbers). 42+14=56. Trap: 48=42+6 (repeats second difference); 54=42+12 (repeats previous difference); 60 adds 18 (wrong).

questions.stem: Find the WRONG term in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, 64
questions.explanation: D is correct. The pattern: differences should be 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 (odd numbers). 2, 5(+3), 10(+5), 17(+7), 26(+9), 37(+11), 50(+13), next should be 50+15=65, not 64. The correct term at position 8 is 65. Trap: students may check the rule only up to 37 or 50 and assume 64 is correct; or they may find the series n²+1 (1²+1=2, 2²+1=5, 3²+1=10... 8²+1=65), confirming 64 is wrong.
